children: Iqbal, a senior advisor at Egon Zehnder and ChrysCapital, will serve a five-year term ending August 7, 2031

Britannia Industries shareholders have approved the appointment of Sonny Iqbal as a non-executive independent director, with the resolution receiving 99.72 per cent of the votes cast in its favour. The postal ballot process concluded on November 6, 2026.

Iqbal’s appointment is effective from August 8, 2026, for a five-year term ending August 7, 2031. He is a senior advisor at Egon Zehnder and ChrysCapital, with professional experience spanning leadership advisory, family businesses and corporate management.
The resolution received strong backing across shareholder categories, although the extent of support varied.

Promoters and promoter group shareholders voted unanimously in favour, with 12.17 crore votes supporting the appointment and none opposing it. Institutional public shareholders recorded 99.26 per cent support, with 7.20 crore votes in favour and 5.33 lakh against.
Among public non-institutional shareholders, 90.14 per cent of votes supported the resolution. This category recorded 1.24 lakh votes in favour and 13,628 against.
Overall, the appointment received 19.38 crore votes in favour, against 5.46 lakh votes opposing it, taking the approval level to 99.72 per cent.
Iqbal’s experience in leadership and family business advisory

Iqbal brings experience across executive search, family enterprise advisory and financial services. At Egon Zehnder, he spent 27 years helping establish the firm’s offices in New Delhi, Bengaluru and Mumbai. He also co-founded its global Family Business Advisory Practice.

He currently serves as a senior advisor to ChrysCapital, one of India’s prominent private equity firms. His earlier professional experience includes senior roles with the Oberoi Group across India, the United Kingdom and the Middle East, as well as managing American Express’s financial services business in India.

Iqbal holds a BA (Hons) degree from St. Stephen’s College, University of Delhi, an MBA in Marketing from the University of Surrey in the UK, and a postgraduate diploma from the Oberoi Centre of Learning and Development.
The company has stated that Iqbal is not related to any of its existing directors and has not been debarred by SEBI or any other regulatory authority.
While the overall approval was decisive, the voting pattern showed a relatively higher level of opposition among public non-institutional shareholders.

Nearly 9.86 per cent of votes cast in this category were against the appointment, compared with 0.74 per cent opposition among institutional investors. Promoter and promoter group shareholders recorded no dissent.

The resolution's overall approval was therefore supported by near-unanimous promoter backing and strong institutional support, even as a section of public non-institutional investors voted against Iqbal’s appointment.
